body:
> Flagged by the operator on 2026-09-02, from GitHub's changelog:
> https://github.blog/changelog/2026-09-01-github-cli-media-in-issues-pull-requests-and-comments/
>
> *"GitHub CLI now has a repeatable `--attach` flag that uploads a local image or video. Reference it inline in
> an issue, pull request, or comment body. Available now to all users on GitHub across all plans."*
>
> This card is an **investigation**, not a decision to build. The question is whether hkb should be able to
> attach media, and what it would cost.

## Why

The protocol is text, everywhere. A worker's result comment (`<!-- kb-result -->`) carries `summary`, `metadata`
and `artifacts[]`; a review record is prose; `hkb graph` is the only visual output and only because GitHub
renders mermaid. So a card whose *subject* is visual can be described and never shown.

That gap has already cost something measurable. #130 recorded a worker on `french-tech-homies/pipao-v2` that
could not reach the `react-aria` MCP server, built the components from training knowledge instead, and said
nothing — **and the output looked fine**. A screenshot in the result comment is exactly what would have made
that visible to a human reading the card. The same repo's board is full of cards whose acceptance is visual: a
component kit re-synced to a design system, an admin page, a marketing page that fails SSR.

There is also a hook already in the protocol waiting for this. `hkb finish --artifacts a,b` exists and is
validated (`assertPayload`, `src/lifecycle.js:173`) — it takes a list of strings and records them in the result
comment. Today those are names of things a reader cannot see. `--attach` is what would make an artifact an
artifact.

## What to investigate — and the constraint that decides it

- **hkb never calls `gh issue` / `gh pr`.** CLAUDE.md is explicit: *"never call `gh issue`/`gh pr` sub-commands
  for board state — use `gh api`"*, and `src/gh.js:12` repeats it (`ghCmd` is for repo detection and doctor,
  "never board state"). `--attach` is a `gh issue comment` / `gh pr comment` flag. **So the first question is
  not "should we" but "can we without breaking the rule that keeps the backend swappable."**
  - Does the CLI flag wrap a REST endpoint hkb could call directly? If media upload has an API surface, this is
    an ordinary `gh api` call and the rule is untouched.
  - If it is CLI-only, the honest options are a narrow, documented exception for *media only* (never board
    state), or not doing it. Say which, with the reasoning, rather than quietly widening `gh.js`.
- **Who would attach, and would they be allowed to?** A worker's launch is `--permission-mode dontAsk` with an
  allow-list; `Bash(gh pr *)` is granted and `gh issue comment` is not. Whatever shape this takes has to work
  from inside a worker, or it is a feature only humans can use — which is most of the value gone.
- **What is worth attaching, concretely.** Do not build a general upload. The candidates the board already
  implies: a screenshot supporting a `completed` result on a visual card; a before/after on a
  `changes_requested` reason; the web board's own view on an operator's review record.
- **Cost and failure modes.** Uploads are not free, not conditional-GET-able, and can fail independently of the
  comment. A result comment that fails because an image upload failed would be worse than no image — the
  terminal verb must never depend on it.
- **Portability.** The protocol is meant to be backend-neutral. An attachment that only exists on GitHub is
  fine as an enhancement and wrong as a requirement; whatever lands must degrade to today's text.

## Done when

- [ ] It is established whether media upload is reachable through `gh api`, or is CLI-only.
- [ ] A decision is recorded — build, or do not build, with the reason — and if building, which of the concrete
      cases above is in scope.
- [ ] If it is CLI-only and worth doing, the exception to the `gh api` rule is written down where the rule is,
      not buried in a commit.
- [ ] Whatever ships, a failed upload never fails a terminal verb, and a board with no attachments reads exactly
      as it does today.
goal: A decision is recorded on whether media upload is reachable via gh api or CLI-only, whether a dontAsk worker could use it, which concrete cases are in scope, and how a failed upload stays unable to fail a terminal verb
title: Investigate gh --attach: whether a worker can show its work, and whether hkb can use it without breaking the gh api rule
